an_err_login_setting.message: Allow the Chrome login above first.

an_note_truncated.message: Only the latest $1 reels were analyzed (limit).

an_note_missing.message: $1 reels have hidden view counts and are left out of the statistics.

an_no_views.message: No view counts available for this profile.

an_tip_mean.message: Arithmetic mean. A few viral reels can pull it up a lot.

an_tip_median.message: Half of the reels have fewer views, half have more. The best 'normal' value for skewed data.

an_tip_typical.message: Interquartile range: 50% of the reels fall inside it.

an_tip_viral.message: Views at least this many times what is typical for this profile at the time it was posted. Statistically about the top 2% on any profile; never less than 3×.

an_tip_top10.message: How much of the total the best 10% of reels collect.

an_tip_er.message: Raw engagement rate: (likes + comments) ÷ views. On real profiles it rises with views (the algorithm pushes reels people react to), so compare it with 'ER vs expected'.

an_group_outliers.message: Group the top 5% into the last bar

an_legend_bars.message: Number of reels in the interval

an_click_bar.message: Click a bar to list its reels.

an_ins_dense.message: $1 of the reels fall between $2 and $3 views.

an_ins_skew.message: The average ($1) is pulled up by a few hits; the median ($2) is the better 'normal' value.

an_ins_viral.message: $1 reels are viral for this profile (≥ $2 typical views) and bring $3 of all views.

an_ins_no_viral.message: No reel is statistically viral for this profile: results are fairly even.

an_ins_top10.message: The top $1 reels (10%) collect $2 of all views.

an_ins_volatile.message: Views vary a lot between reels (hit-driven profile).

an_ins_trend_up.message: The newer half of the reels has a $1 higher median than the older half.

an_ins_trend_down.message: The newer half of the reels has a $1 lower median than the older half.

an_tip_score.message: Views ÷ typical views of the reels posted around the same time ($1). z = $2: how many robust standard deviations above (or below) typical.

an_queued.message: $1 reels queued → $2 (one every few seconds to avoid Instagram limits).

set_meta.message: Also save a metadata JSON file next to each download (off = only images and videos)

an_cached.message: Saved result from $1 (no new request was made). Press Analyze to refresh the numbers.

set_compat.message: Compatibility mode: only H.264/H.265 videos (open everywhere, e.g. QuickTime) — may be a lower resolution on Instagram. Off = maximum quality (H.264/H.265 still preferred when the resolution is the same).

an_click_bar_date.message: Click a bar → that period's reels in the table

an_act_note.message: Times are in your computer's time zone. Only analyzed reels are counted (regular posts and stories are not included).

an_tip_vpd.message: Daily views: views ÷ days since posting. Shows which reel (product) is hot right now.

an_tip_gap.message: Time between two consecutive reels. The median ignores a few long pauses, so it shows the usual pace better.

an_tip_active.message: Share of days with at least one reel.

an_ai_pace.message: Posts about $1 reels a week; usually $2 between two reels.

an_ai_trend_restart.message: No posts in the previous 30 days, $1 reels in the last 30 — the profile is active again (maybe a new product test).

an_ai_trend_up.message: Pace is rising: $1 reels in the last 30 days vs $2 in the 30 before. Often a new product test or pushing a winner.

an_ai_trend_down.message: Pace is dropping: $1 reels in the last 30 days vs $2 in the 30 before.

an_ai_trend_flat.message: Pace is steady: $1 reels in the last 30 days vs $2 in the 30 before.

an_ai_inactive.message: The last reel was $1 days ago — the store may have paused or moved to another platform.

an_ai_best_day.message: Best results on $1: median $2 views ($3 reels) vs $4 overall.

an_ai_best_time.message: Best time slot $1: median $2 views ($3 reels).

an_ai_multi_worse.message: Days with 2+ reels get median $1 views vs $2 on single-post days — posting more splits the views.

an_ai_multi_better.message: Days with 2+ reels get median $1 views vs $2 on single-post days — posting more doesn't hurt this profile.

an_ai_multi_same.message: No real difference in median views between 2+ post days ($1) and single-post days ($2).

an_ai_regular.message: Posting is very regular — likely a planned or scheduled posting calendar.

an_ai_bursty.message: Posting is irregular: bursts of reels, then pauses (campaigns or product-test waves).

an_ai_hot.message: Hottest reel of the last 30 days: ~$1 views/day ($2) — “$3”.

an_ai_truncated.message: Only the latest $1 reels were analyzed, so the start date is not when the profile started. Raise the limit for a longer history.

an_thr_date.message: No filter for dates: all $2 reels, newest first.

an_thr_hint.message: Type a number: 10K, 1.5M, 2500. For ER in percent: 5 = 5%.

an_tip_strong.message: Clearly above this profile's typical views (about the top 16%), but not viral.

an_stat_winner_sub.message: strong reach + more engagement than that reach usually gets

an_tip_winner.message: Strong or viral reach AND engagement above what reels with that many views normally get on this profile (z ≥ 1). People watched it and reacted: the best hint of a product with demand.

an_tip_high_er.message: Engagement far above what is expected for the reel's views (z ≥ 2, at least 20 likes + comments). Comment outliers often mean questions like 'where can I buy this?'.

an_method_title.message: How are Viral, Strong and Winner calculated?

an_method_few.message: At least 8 reels with view counts are needed for a statistical classification.

an_method_why.message: Why not '3× median' or '2× average'? Views on social video are heavy-tailed (a few reels get most of the views). A fixed multiplier then means something different on every profile: on a steady account '3× median' is almost never reached, on a volatile one it labels 1 in 5 reels viral. The average is pulled up by the hits themselves, so 'above average' is simply the top ~30%. So this tool measures how unusual a reel is for this profile, on a log scale, with outlier-resistant statistics.

an_method_baseline_local.message: Typical views = the median of the ~30 reels posted closest in time to each reel. A growing (or shrinking) account is compared with its own level at that moment, not with its whole history.

an_method_baseline_global.message: Typical views = the median of all analyzed reels (fewer than 20 reels, so no time-local baseline).

an_method_tiers.message: This profile's spread (robust standard deviation of log views, from the median absolute deviation) is $1. Strong = at least $2 typical views (z ≥ 1, about the top 16%). Viral = at least $3 typical views (z ≥ 2, about the top 2%). Viral is never below 3× and strong never below 1.5×, so a steady account doesn't call a small bump viral.

an_method_eng.message: Engagement is judged against reach, because on real profiles they move together: here log(likes + comments) grows with log(views) with slope $1 (1.0 would mean the engagement rate doesn't depend on views; above 1 = reels with more views also get a higher rate). A robust (Theil–Sen) line gives the expected engagement for every view count; 'ER vs expected' is the difference from that line, and its robust z decides High engagement (z ≥ 2) and Winner (strong or viral reach + z ≥ 1). Comments get their own line (slope $2: below 1 = the comment rate falls as reach grows).

an_method_new.message: Reels younger than 3 days are still collecting views: they are marked NEW, left out of the baselines and never called weak.

an_ins_winner.message: $1 winner candidates: strong reach and above-typical engagement. Look at these products first.

an_ins_viral_low_er.message: $1 viral reels have clearly weaker engagement than usual: watched (a strong hook) but not acted on.

an_ins_talk.message: $1 reels get unusually many comments per view: read those comments for buying questions and objections.

an_sig_viral_tip.message: z = $1 (≥ 2): about the top 2% for this profile.

an_sig_strong_tip.message: z = $1 (≥ 1): about the top 16% for this profile.

an_sig_weak_tip.message: z ≤ −1: clearly below typical for this profile.

an_sig_new_tip.message: Posted less than 3 days ago: still collecting views.

an_sig_winner_tip.message: Strong or viral reach and engagement above what that reach normally gets (z ≥ 1).

an_sig_high_er_tip.message: Engagement $1 vs $2 expected for this reach; z = $3 (≥ 2).

an_sig_talk_tip.message: Comments per view z = $1 (≥ 2) for this reach, and at least 5 comments.

an_viral_legend.message: Viral ≈ (typical views × viral multiple; each reel is compared with reels posted around the same time)

an_tip_eradj.message: Actual engagement $1; expected for a reel with this many views on this profile: $2. Engagement z = $3. Positive = people reacted more than this reach normally brings.

an_method_tail.message: Viral rate on this profile: $1 of reels. A pure log-normal (no real virality) would give about 2%; anything clearly above that is a genuine viral tail.

an_method_dates.message: Instagram's reels list doesn't return post dates any more, so dates are decoded from each reel's shortcode (the media ID contains its creation time). Accurate to the minute for normal posts.

an_rb_sub.message: Pick the period to analyze. Everything below (viral, winners, charts, table) is recalculated for it.

an_rb_period_tip.message: A stretch of regular posting between two pauses.

an_rb_lg_pause.message: Pause (≥ 14 days and ≥ 10× the usual gap)

an_tip_ercell.message: Engagement $1 = like rate $2 ($3 of the engagement) + comment rate $4 ($5 of the engagement). 1 comment per $6 likes.

an_tip_mix.message: Which part of all engagement comes from likes and which from comments (sums over the reels in range). Comments take more effort than a like, so a higher comment share usually means questions, tags of friends or buying interest.

an_tip_rates.message: Total likes and total comments divided by total views of the reels in range. Like rate + comment rate = engagement rate.

an_er_bar_hint.message: hover a cell for the exact split

an_rb_hint.message: Drag the handles or the selected window · click to move the nearest handle · ← → keys (Shift = 7 days)

an_lg_score_hint.message: hover the number for all signals (new, high ER, talked about …)

an_tip_rising.message: Rising: posted $1 ago and already $2 views ($3 typical, ~$4 views per hour). Still collecting views, so the final number will be higher.

an_tip_fresh.message: New: posted $1 ago (~$2 views per hour). Still collecting views; not above the strong line yet.

an_ins_rising.message: $1 new reels (under 3 days old) are already above the strong line and still growing: watch these products now.

an_act_legend_total.message: Total views of all reels posted in that interval

an_heat_tip_single.message: Only 1 reel here: an anecdote, not a pattern.

an_heat_lg_posts.message: Darker = more reels posted at that time

an_heat_lg_above.message: Above typical (median 'vs typical' of the reels posted then; 4× = full green)

an_sum_pooled.message: Pooled (totals ÷ total views, big reels weigh more): $1

an_cancelled.message: $1 downloads cancelled. Files that were already completely saved stay in the folder.

update_failed.message: The update did not finish: $1 Try again, or double-click Update-Windows.bat / Update-Mac.command in your MediaDownloader folder.

update_manual.message: This one time, please update by hand: double-click Update-Windows.bat (Windows) or Update-Mac.command (Mac) in the MediaDownloader folder in your home folder. After that, updates are one click.

an_cap_loading.message: Loading descriptions from Instagram… $1 / $2 (one at a time, to stay under Instagram's limit)

an_cap_stopped_ig.message: Instagram asked to slow down, so loading stopped: wait 10–15 minutes and press the button again to get the rest (loaded ones are remembered).

an_cap_stopped_user.message: Stopped: press the button again to continue (loaded ones are remembered).
